title: Record multispectrum review evidence for merged PR wave (retroactive)
lens: M1 — challenge the single load-bearing assumption; one lens only
load_bearing_assumption: A retroactive, self-administered multispectrum review of nine already-merged PRs produces honest, durable, schema-conformant evidence that strengthens the doctrine.

challenged_assumptions.evidence: PR #17 reviews 9 PRs whose merge commit SHAs are already known (e.g., cdc53bf for PR #1). Every r1 file embeds merge_commit_sha, every audit-chain row is stamped with the IDENTICAL timestamp_unix=1778920055 (batch-emitted, not capture-at-time), and every r2 file's `position` is hard-coded to `concurs_with_synthesis_after_rebuttal`. The reviewer cannot disconfirm consensus because consensus was the input. Confirmation bias is not a risk here; it is the topology.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: Name a single counterfactual the review could have produced. If the answer is `none — the PRs are merged`, the artifact is not review, it is ratification. Reframe as `audit-trail backfill` (per F1/F3) or do nothing.

challenged_assumptions.evidence: F3 found zero immutability binding: audit-chain.jsonl rows carry no prev_hash, no payload_content_sha256, no signature; synthesis_path is a bare relative repo path; no CI lane blocks in-place edits of evidence/debate/pr-*-*.json. The word `chain` in `audit-chain.jsonl` is a misnomer — it is an append-only log with no cryptographic link. Combined with editable evidence files, any future contributor can soften the 64 declared blockers and the audit-chain row stays byte-valid.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: An audit trail without content binding is theater dressed as forensics. Either add prev_event_hash + payload_content_sha256 + a CI lane that re-derives both, or stop calling the file a `chain`.

challenged_assumptions.evidence: A6 (schema_adherence) and F5 (quality) independently confirm that doctrine round_1_independent.required_keys = [reviewer_id, round, change_id, answer, key_claims, uncertainty_areas]. PR #17's r1 files carry NONE of {answer, key_claims, uncertainty_areas} and most omit `round`; they use an ad-hoc shape {summary, findings, considered, rigor, null_finding_reason}. Zero r1 files declare $schema or $id. The PR is internally inconsistent: some r1s include {pr_number, pr_title, merge_commit_sha}, others omit them. `jq empty` (the validation cited in the PR body) catches parse errors, not schema conformance.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: If doctrine schema was followed, A6 would find conformance. It did not. Either ratify a retrospective variant in specs/cross-cutting/multispectrum-review.json with an explicit alias map and version pin, or migrate the 73+ r1 files to the canonical shape. Do not call non-conformant artifacts `doctrine evidence`.

challenged_assumptions.evidence: F1 demonstrated that the policy produced byte-identical r2 files across facets F2-F9 per PR, differing only in {facet_id, facet_name, reviewer_id}. The three round_2_findings bullets share the literal prefix `Round-2 Fn reconciliation preserved consensus finding:`. Every remediation is the same sentence: `Keep the synthesis FixupTask and do not downgrade severity without a new facet-specific evidence file.` Naming_justification across all 171 files is templated. The rule did not prevent automation — it forced humans to perform the automation by hand and call it review. A 30-line jq generator would produce the same artifacts transparently and reproducibly.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: Banning generators while shipping generator-output is the worst of both worlds: opaque provenance, ceremonial labor, and falsified `independent` rebuttals. Replace the blanket ban with an allowlist: evidence emission MAY use a checked-in renderer if its source ships in the diff and inputs are explicit.

challenged_assumptions.evidence: Audit-chain rows declare fixuptasks_recommended summing to 64 (9+2+9+10+2+10+6+6+10) with stable IDs F-PR<N>-NN. F3 verified by grep that the PR diff does NOT touch registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl. The 64 blockers are unfiled in the canonical registry; downstream gates cannot enforce what is not registered. `ACCEPT_WITH_BLOCKING_FIXUPS` is paperwork-only.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: A blocker that no gate consumes is a sticky note, not a blocker. File the 64 rows atomically with PR #17 or add a CI lane that fails when `fixuptask_id` strings in evidence/debate/ reference IDs missing from the registry.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Establishing retroactive consensus_debate_complete events sets no harmful precedent
challenged_assumptions.evidence: F3 attack scenario: a future agent under deadline pressure cites PR #17 as precedent — `we merged PR-X without consensus debate; we will append the debate evidence in a follow-up`. Once normalized, the pre-merge multispectrum gate becomes optional decoration. Nothing in the PR body acknowledges this inversion or constrains future use. The doctrine intent is to gate merges; this PR inverts the control direction.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: If retroactive backfill is legitimate exactly once for pre-doctrine merges, say so explicitly in the PR body and an ADR, and add a CI lane that fails when a consensus_debate_complete event's timestamp_unix exceeds the PR merge commit timestamp without an explicit backfill_authorization ADR reference.

load_bearing_failure: The PR's single load-bearing assumption — that retroactive self-administered review on already-merged PRs produces honest, durable, doctrine-conformant evidence — fails on all four sub-claims simultaneously: (1) the review cannot disconfirm because outcomes are known and r2 `concurs` is hard-coded; (2) the `audit chain` is an unhashed text log over editable files, so the record can be silently rewritten; (3) the r1 shape diverges from doctrine schema with no alias ratification; (4) the no-scripts policy produced byte-identical hand-typed templates that pretend to be independent rebuttals. The retroactive framing is what makes each of these failures invisible: nothing was at stake, so nothing was challenged.
recommended_followups: Reframe PR #17 in the body and an ADR as `pre-doctrine audit-trail backfill (one-shot)`, not `multispectrum review`; add CI lane forbidding post-merge consensus_debate_complete events without explicit backfill authorization.
Add prev_event_hash + payload_content_sha256 to audit-chain.jsonl rows; add CI lane that re-derives both and fails on mismatch; pin synthesis_path with synthesis_path_sha256.

Ratify a retrospective r1 variant in specs/cross-cutting/multispectrum-review.json with an explicit alias map and $schema pin, OR migrate the 73+ r1 files to the canonical {answer, key_claims, uncertainty_areas, round} shape.

File the 64 F-PR<N>-NN FixupTasks in registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl atomically with PR #17; add CI lane that fails on referenced-but-unregistered fixuptask_id strings under evidence/debate/.

Replace the blanket no-shell/no-Python/no-.mjs continuation rule with an allowlist for checked-in renderers (e.g., scripts/evidence/emit-r2.jq) whose source ships in the diff and whose inputs are explicit; OR add a sanctioned `{round:2, no_new_findings:true, reason:...}` aggregate shape so reviewers stop manufacturing templated rebuttals.
verdict: approve-with-fixups (PR already merged; fixups land on doctrine, schema, audit-chain integrity, registry filing, and the no-scripts rule)
